result.title: Attention Is Not Relevance: Challenging the Causality of Attention in Autonomous Driving
result.summary: Attention has become one of the most widely adopted solutions for estimating the relevance of surrounding objects and interpreting an autonomous vehicle's driving decisions. However, its ability to capture the causal impact of individual input elements on an AI model's output has long been discussed in the literature, particularly in the Natural Language Processing (NLP) domain. This work brings this discussion into the autonomous driving domain by analyzing the accuracy of attention in estimating the impact of an input object on an autonomous vehicle's driving, i.e., its relevance. To this end, we compare different attention-based relevance estimation methods against a causal reference of object relevance obtained through counterfactual analysis. We perform our analysis on more than 80,000 synthetic driving scenes using an autonomous vehicle based on PlanT 2.0, a state-of-the-art Transformer-based model for object-level planning. Results show that attention provides a correlational rather than causal indication of object relevance. Attention-based relevance estimation methods do not consistently identify all relevant objects and tend to incorrectly classify as relevant objects with little or no impact on the vehicle's driving. In particular, results show that attention can effectively identify relevant objects in simple single-lane, straight-road scenarios, but its accuracy degrades in more complex settings, such as multi-lane roads and intersections. These findings highlight the limitations of attention as a proxy for object relevance, calling for novel methods able to accurately capture the causal impact of individual objects on the vehicle's driving and distinguish it from correlational associations.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在自动驾驶场景中检验 attention 是否能反映输入对象对模型输出的因果影响：基于 PlanT 2.0 对 8 万余个合成驾驶场景做反事实分析，得到对象相关性的因果参照，并与多种基于 attention 的相关性估计方法比较。结果显示 attention 只提供相关性而非因果性指示，且在多车道与路口等复杂场景中准确度下降。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用反事实扰动构造因果参照、再检验 attention 是否对齐」的评估思路，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 视觉证据筛选与贡献分配是否真具因果作用，而非仅反映注意力或相关性结构；注意该文非 VLM 推理研究，迁移属推测。
